title: Polynomial-factor hardness of the closest vector problem
abstract: Formalizes polynomial-factor NP-hardness of the closest vector problem through an explicit reduction from 3-SAT. The development also derives NP-hardness of binary nearest codeword, binary syndrome decoding, and finite p-norm variants of GapCVP. It includes machine-level polynomial-time bounds, binary encodings, affine systems, Reed--Solomon-style interpolation, and the lattice and coding-theory reductions needed by the final results.

informal.GapCVP.Comparator.gapCVP400IsNPHard: GapCVP in the Euclidean norm with approximation factor n^(1/400), where n is the lattice dimension, is NP-hard as a promise problem: every NP language reduces in polynomial time to the promise problem on encoded well-formed instances (positive dimension, nonsingular integer basis, positive rational radius) with an integer target, whose YES instances have a lattice vector within the radius of the target and whose NO instances have every lattice vector at distance greater than n^(1/400) times the radius.
informal.GapCVP.Comparator.binaryNearestCodewordI: Binary nearest codeword is NP-hard as a promise problem.
informal.GapCVP.Comparator.binarySyndromeDecoding: Binary syndrome decoding is NP-hard as a promise problem.
informal.GapCVP.Comparator.finitePNormGapCVPIsNPH: For every rational p at least one, the finite p-norm version of GapCVP is NP-hard as a promise problem.
